name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing across multiple stable and beta tracks. The current latest stable release is v0.64.1 (released October 7, 2025), with v0.65.0-beta available as a pre-release (October 13, 2025). Long-term support patches continue on older branches such as v0.63.x and v0.58.x. Both open-source (v0.x) and enterprise (v1.x) editions are available as Docker images and JAR downloads. Release notes are available at https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Dual-licensed: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license.
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases across stable and beta tracks in September–October 2025.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com.
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, SQLite, MongoDB, Druid, Oracle, Presto/Trino, Spark SQL, and more via drivers.

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers superior visualization capabilities and enterprise support but is proprietary, expensive, and lacks Metabase's open-source flexibility.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Lightdash integrates tightly with dbt for a metrics-as-code workflow, making it more developer-friendly but less accessible to non-technical users than Metabase.
